result: # Connected World kit: code inspection report Scope: everything in `kit/.../Wishweave-Connected-World-Kit/code/` (shortened to `KIT/` below). I modified nothing under `/home/user/threadgame`. My scratch probes are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-threadgame/131a49c9-f445-5dda-9dd9-fdcc5c2be76a/scratchpad/inspect/` (`handed.mjs`, `gest.mjs`). ## 0. Test run (from repo root, absolute paths) `node --test /home/user/threadgame/kit/connected/Wishweave-Connected-World-Kit/code/touch-input.test.mjs /home/user/threadgame/kit/connected/Wishweave-Connected-World-Kit/code/route-motion.test.mjs` on Node v22.22.0: ``` 1..34 # tests 34 # suites 0 # pass 34 # fail 0 # cancelled 0 # skipped 0 # todo 0 ``` This matches the kit's own record in `docs/VERIFICATION.json:5-7`. The split is 26 touch-input tests and 8 route-motion tests. ## 1. Public API and behaviour ### touch-input.mjs (browser ES module, no dependencies) **Constants** - `DEFAULTS` (`touch-input.mjs:2-6`): ```js { swipeWidthRatio: 0.08, swipeMin: 24, swipeMax: 72, axisDominance: 1.2, tapSlop: 10, tapDuration: 200, doubleTapInterval: 320, doubleTapDistance: 24 } ``` - `INTENTS` (`:8-14`), all frozen: - `left` = `{type:'steer',direction:-1}` - `right` = `{type:'steer',direction:1}` - `jump` = `{type:'jump'}` - `togglePlayerBrake` = `{type:'toggle-player-brake'}` - `toggleGlobalPause` = `{type:'toggle-global-pause'}` (only a button emits this, never a gesture) **Swipe threshold** `swipeThreshold(w)` (`:16-20`): `clamp(0.08*w, 24, 72)` CSS px. An invalid or zero width falls back to 320, giving 25.6. Measured: 32.96 px at 412 wide, 28.8 px at 360 wide. The current game uses 36 px (`game/src/ui/input.js:30`). **Classifier** `classifyGesture({dx,dy,duration,maxDistance,viewportWidth})` (`:23-32`): - **tap**: `duration ≤ 200` and `max(maxDistance, |d|) ≤ 10` (`:26`). - **left/right**: `|dx| ≥ thr` and `|dx| ≥ 1.2|dy|` (`:29`). - **jump** (up) or **reserved** (down): the same test on the vertical axis (`:30`). - **none**: everything else. - It uses the net displacement at release. `maxDistance` only matters for the tap test, so a drag-return gives `none`. **Gesture machine** `createGestureMachine(opts)` (`:38-107`) has no DOM dependency. Each method returns `[]` or `[intent]`. - **Clock**: time must be a finite monotonic number. Non-finite throws `TypeError`; a backwards step is clamped (`:42-46`). - **`down`** (`:54-67`): - A duplicate pointer id is a no-op. - `ignored:true` or a second contact clears the stroke and the pending tap and sets `blocked`. - **`move`** (`:68-70`) only updates the position and `maxDistance`. It never emits anything. - **`up`** (`:71-94`): this is the only point where a stroke resolves, once. - **Double tap**: the second tap's release is within 320 ms of the first tap's release, and its start is within 24 px of the first tap's start (`:84-85`). A single tap does nothing. After a pair, a third tap starts a new pair (`:86`). - Any non-tap result, including `none` and `reserved`, clears the pending tap (`:92`). - `blocked` clears only when every tracked pointer has lifted (`:78`). - **`cancel(id,{retainPointer})`** (`:95-101`): clears the stroke and the pending tap. With `retainPointer`, the pointer stays tracked, so the machine stays blocked until that pointer actually goes up. - **`reset()`** (`:102-105`): clears everything. **DOM adapter** `attachTouchInput(surface, onIntent, opts)` (`:112-158`) returns `{reset, dispose}`. - **Listeners**: on `document`, capture phase, `passive:false` (`:119-122`). - **UI exclusion**: selector `'[data-ui],button,a,input,select,textarea,[contenteditable="true"],[role="button"]'`, checked against the composed path and `closest` (`:116-117,128`). - **A down is ignored when** (`:131-132`): - it starts outside the surface, or - it starts on UI, or - `button !== 0`, or - it is a non-primary touch. This guards a second finger that arrives after a `reset()`. - **Accepted downs**: `preventDefault` and `setPointerCapture` (`:134-137`). - **Moves**: coalesced events are replayed (`:139-144`). - **Cancellation**: - `pointercancel` → `cancel(id)` (`:148`). - `lostpointercapture` → `cancel(id,{retainPointer:true})` (`:151`). This is harmless after a normal `pointerup` because the id is already gone (test `:120-129`). - **Lifecycle**: window `blur` and a hidden `visibilitychange` call `reset()` (`:152-153`). `dispose()` removes every listener and resets (`:156`). - **Time source**: `opts.now` overrides it (default `performance.now`, `:115`). ### route-motion.mjs **`sampleRoad(route, distance, lateral=0, bodyRadius=0.35)`** (`:6-23`) - Validates its inputs and throws `TypeError` on bad ones (`:8`). It also throws if `s` does not strictly increase (`:13`). - Clamps `s` to `[first.s, last.s]` (`:9`), then finds the segment by binary search (`:10-11`). - Interpolates the centre linearly. `forward` is the normalised lerp of the two tangents (`:16`). - `right = unit([f.z, 0, -f.x])` (`:17`) and `normal = f × right` (`:18`). There is no bank. - `width` uses each point's width or falls back to `route.width` (`:19`). - **Lateral clamp**: `limit = max(0, width/2 - bodyRadius)` (`:20-21`). That is ±2.65 m on main (width 6) and ±0.95 m on the branch (width 2.6). - Returns `{s, center, position, forward, right, normal, width, lateral, heading: atan2(f.x,f.z), mainS}`. - `mainS` is the lerp of the points' `mainS` on a branch, and `s` itself on main, whose points have no `mainS` (`:22`). **`advanceRun(state{s,speed,phase,braked}, dt, {runSpeed, accelerationTime=0.3, brakingTime=0.22, strideLength=1.4, paused=false, routeLength=Infinity})`** (`:25-38`) - Exact constant-acceleration integration within a step: speed changes for part of `dt`, then cruises (`:30-35`). - Acceleration is `runSpeed/accelerationTime`; deceleration is `runSpeed/brakingTime`. - `paused` or `dt===0` returns the state unchanged with `distanceMoved:0` (`:29`). - At `routeLength` the runner clamps, speed becomes 0 and the overshoot is dropped (`:36-37`). - `phase = frac(phase + d/strideLength)`, so the stride is driven by distance. **`chaseTargets(route, distance, lateral, {behind=5.5, height=3.2, lookAhead=7, targetHeight=0.8})`** (`:40-46`) - Camera position = player position − forward·5.5 + 3.2 Y. Look target = the road sample at `s+7` (same lateral) + 0.8 Y. - No smoothing and no collision. **Branches**: there is no graph code. The only branch support is `sampleRoad(branchObj, localS)` plus the `mainS` field. `ROUTE-MOTION.txt:16` tells the host to switch from main `s` to branch `s` at the fork, back to main `endS` at the rejoin, and to use `mainS` for race progress. ## 2. Gaps against CLAUDIA-PROMPT.txt | Requirement | What the kit provides | What is missing | |---|---|---| | **Branch selection window** (prompt:16, MOTION:11) | `route.json` gives fork s=81.4266, rejoin s=97.4122 and `connectivity` | No window, no announcement and no side/direction field. Fork position: branch lateral is 0 at branch s=0, 1.24 m at s=3, 2.6 m at s=5, 5.0 m max at s≈10. Its width (2.6) also tightens the lateral clamp from ±2.65 to ±0.95, so switching "at the exact connection" from a main lateral of +2.65 snaps the runner by up to 1.7 m. A world-space or projection-based handoff is needed; the kit has no `project()`. | | **"Valid shorter route"** (prompt:24) | — | The only branch is longer: 19.543 m against 15.986 m of main, about 0.7 s slower at 5 m/s. A shortcut needs new data or a different reason to take the branch. | | **Jump physics** | none (`ROUTE-MOTION.txt:3`) | Keep the existing sim: `jumpTime 0.68`, `sin(πt)`, `inputBufferTime 0.15`, `jumpAirborneAbove 0.3` (`core/ww.js:19-21`, `sim/race.js:576-580`). Lift along road up/normal per `MOTION-AND-CAMERA.txt:9`. Jumping while stopped must happen in place and must not resume running. | | **Brake** | `advanceRun` brakes in 0.22 s | The current `purlAccel` is 9 m/s² (`ww.js:17`), which takes about 0.56 s to stop from 5 m/s; the kit requires 0.18–0.25 s. There is no `braked` flag in the sim yet. | | **Loop AI** | independent states only (test `route-motion.test.mjs:22-24`) | No route decisions, reaction timing or mistakes. Port `sim/loop-ai.js` (react/hesitate/hop-miss/stumble/drop, all seeded) onto route `s`/`mainS`. | | **Collisions** | landmark `footprintRadius` and markers only | No colliders (`scenery/README.md:3`). The fork and rejoin decks overlap, and the kit says to bake a collision union. Snagling is a marker only (`route.json spawnPositions.snaglingPlaceholder`). | | **Pull-lesson coexistence** | down = `reserved` | See below. | | **Stitch taps** | single taps are discarded (`touch-input.mjs:83-90`) | The current tap-to-open stitches (`input.js:152,165-172`, `race.js:555-558`) would stop working. If any stitch stays tappable, add a `tap{x,y}` intent. A tap that hits a stitch target must be consumed and must not arm a double tap. | | **Pause** | `paused` flag in `advanceRun`; the adapter resets on blur and when the page is hidden | The machine has no idea of pause. The host must drop intents while paused (`README.md:37`) and call `reset()` when the pause screen or a mode changes (`README:24`). This fits the current lifecycle (`ARCHITECTURE.md §9`). | | **Determinism / fixed 1/60 step** | `advanceRun` is pure (verified) | At 1/60: braking from 4 m/s covers 0.43999999999999984 m (exact answer 0.44); 0→4 m/s takes 18 steps and 0.600000 m; two replays of a 6000-step run with brake toggling were identical. The gesture machine runs on wall-clock `performance.now()` but stays on the input side, so the sim remains deterministic for a given intent sequence. Intents must still be queued into `race.input()` between steps, as now. No RNG is involved. | | **Swipe latency** | resolves on release only (`README:20`, `:68-70`) | A 300 ms swipe fires at 300 ms. The current input fires as soon as the threshold is reached (`input.js:131-134`). This matters for branch windows and jump timing; consider firing early once the threshold is crossed. There is also no maximum swipe duration: holding 2 s and then dragging 45 px still steers. | **Pull-lesson coexistence.** I checked what the kit machine does with pull-style strokes at 412 px width (`gest.mjs`): - A straight downward drag of 100 px over 800 ms → `reserved`, no intent. Safe. - A diagonal pull (dx −50, dy +40) → **steer left**. - Pulling down 100 px, then releasing 40 px above the start point → **jump**. - Two quick touches on the gold loop → **toggle-player-brake**. The current pull gesture is never a tap or a swipe (`input.js:16-21,89-99`; `PULL-STITCH.md:62`). The gold loop is drawn on the canvas, so `data-ui` exclusion cannot apply to it. To make them coexist: 1. Add a start hook to the ported adapter, such as `classifyStart(x,y)` using `pullHit`. 2. When a press starts on a pull target, give it to the existing pull tracker and call `machine.down({...,ignored:true})`. That also clears pending taps and blocks other gestures until the finger lifts. 3. Keep the sim-side guard `if (st.tutorial) return;` (`race.js:570`) and extend it to brake toggles. 4. Call `reset()` when the lesson hold starts and ends. 5. Never mount both adapters on the canvas (`README:75`). **Edge cases I verified** - **Handedness (most important).** `right = [f.z,0,-f.x]` is +X when facing +Z. glTF is right-handed with −X as right. I projected `sampleRoad(s, ±1)` through three r147 (`game/vendor/three.min.js`) with a `PerspectiveCamera` aimed with `chaseTargets`. At s = 5, 40, 81, 120 and 180, **lateral +1 lands on the screen's left** (for example, at s=5 the NDC x is −0.897 against +0.722 for lateral −1). - The data uses the same convention (`generate_course.py:47`; `scenery/README.md:17` calls it "right"). Collectible positions reproduce exactly with it (error 0.0000 with +Y hover). - So the data is consistent, but `INTENTS.right` (+1) must map to lateral −1 in a three.js render. Alternatively, negate the vector in one place. - The branch sits at kit lateral +0…+5, so on screen it is to the **left** of the main road. - **Look-ahead clamps at a route's end** (`:42-43`, via `:9`). At the branch end, the target stops at the branch end instead of continuing onto main. At the finish, the target is directly above Purl (horizontal distance 0), so the camera looks straight down. The look-ahead has to sample across the route graph and past the finish. - `chaseTargets` re-clamps lateral with `bodyRadius` 0.35, whatever the host uses. - The camera's "behind" offset follows the current tangent, not the road. It strays at most 0.64 m (horizontal) from the centreline on this layout. - **Branch overshoot.** With `routeLength` set to the branch length, `advanceRun` sets speed to 0 and loses the leftover distance (0.0234 m in one 1/60 step). For handoff, pass `Infinity` and convert `s − branch.length + endS` yourself. - **Capture loss without a `pointerup`.** The machine stays blocked until that pointer lifts or `reset()` is called (verified). This is intended, but the host must call `reset()` on mode changes. - **Taps.** A tap must be ≤200 ms, against the current game's 300 ms (`input.js:29`). A 201 ms touch counts as `none` and cancels a pending double tap. This needs device tuning. ## 3. Integration recommendation: classic scripts on `WW`, not ES modules **Why** - `ARCHITECTURE.md §1-2` requires classic scripts on `globalThis.WW` that also open from `file://`. - `tests/unit/load.cjs:20-33` loads `src/(core|data|sim)` scripts from `index.html` with `vm.runInThisContext`, which cannot evaluate ES modules. - ES modules would load in the WebView: the androidx.webkit 1.14.0 `MimeUtil` maps both `js` and `mjs` to `text/javascript` (checked with `javap`, switch cases 33 and 34 → offset 1506). They would still fail from `file://` (kit `README.md:3`) and in the Node sim tests. - House style: `game/src` has no arrow functions, `?.`, `??`, `.at(`, or `catch {}` (grep found 0). The kit uses all of them. **Port with the logic unchanged (syntax only)** - `game/src/core/gesture.js` → `WW.gesture = {DEFAULTS, INTENTS, swipeThreshold, classify, createMachine}`, with all of `touch-input.mjs:2-107`. Putting it in `core` lets `load.cjs` test it in Node. - `game/src/ui/touch.js` → `WW.ui.attachTouch`, porting `:112-158`: capture-phase document listeners, coalesced moves, capture loss with the pointer retained, blur/visibility reset, the `isPrimary` guard and the UI selector. Add: - the pull-target start hook; - an optional `tap{x,y}` intent; - the keyboard handling from `input.js:174-200`. This replaces the pointer half of `createInput`. Keep `cancelPull`/`active` for `main.js:191,213`. - `game/src/core/route.js` → `WW.route = {sample, advance, chase}`, with `sampleRoad` and `advanceRun` as written and `chaseTargets` only as a starting point. **Rewrite** - Fix the lateral sign: either the right vector or the intent mapping. - Add a route-graph wrapper: racer `{routeId, s, lateral, braked, …}`, progress as `mainS`, fork/rejoin handoff with lateral blending, overflow carry, and a junction window with side selection. - Look-ahead that crosses the graph, plus time-based camera damping in the renderer (not the sim). - Brake, jump and the Snagling contact in `sim/race.js`. - Loop AI re-targeted onto the route. - Convert `route.json` into a script (`game/src/data/route.js`, `WW.ROUTE = …`, 135 KB), because `fetch` of JSON fails under `file://` and `load.cjs` only runs JS. - Port the kit's 34 tests into `tests/unit/*.test.cjs` through `load()`, and add tests for the pull/tap/brake interactions. ## 4.
